title: Find Your People: Support Resources for Military Families

sections.heading: Why Support Matters
sections.markdown:
Military life can be challenging, but community support reduces stress, strengthens families, and builds lasting bonds.

A military family is made stronger by the village it builds.

sections.heading: Build Your Village
sections.markdown:
* Attend military or community family events.
* Join the New Parent Support Program playgroups or the Family Advocacy Program parenting class.
* Attend chapel or faith-based events or family support groups.
* Exchange contact info with neighbors, especially during PCS season.
* Get involved in the Parent Board at your child's [child development center (CDC)](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/cdc) or [school-age care (SAC)](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/child-and-youth/school-age-care) program.
* Host monthly potlucks or game nights with other families.
* Start a coffee or walking club with other parents.
* Volunteer or enroll your children in youth sports.
* Connect with the [Exceptional Family Member Program](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/efmp) for additional resources and attend their family events.
* Join family involvement activities at your child's CDC or SAC program to connect, play, and grow together.

sections.heading: Support Resources
sections.markdown:
* [Family Advocacy Program (FAP)](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/fap) offers workshops and classes for parenting, relationships, stress, and anger management to maintain healthy family relationships.
* [New Parent Support Program (NPSP)](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/npsp) provides a range of support for parents of children 0-5 years old, including home visitation, playgroups, parenting classes, and baby boot camp.
* [Child and Youth Programs (CYP)](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/cyp) provide high-quality child care and recreational activities for children and teens from birth to 18 years old, including child development centers, school-age care programs, family childcare, and a variety of youth and teen programs.
* Other [Marine Corps Community Services (MCCS)](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/) programs offer free or low-cost activities.

sections.heading: Online Communities & Apps
sections.markdown:
* [Military OneSource](https://www.militaryonesource.mil/): 24/7 support for parenting, relationships, and mental health.
* Babies on the Homefront mobile app: Articles, videos, toolkits, etc. to support military families.
* Facebook groups: Local military spouse communities, deployment support circles.
* [MilitaryMomCollective.com](https://MilitaryMomCollective.com): Articles, forums, and shared experiences from fellow parents.

sections.heading: Take the First Step
sections.markdown:
Military life isn't meant to be faced alone.

Strength grows through connection, and support begins with simple actions—showing up, reaching out, and getting involved.

Whether navigating parenthood, settling into a new duty station, or building friendships, community resources are in place to help families thrive.

Now is the time to build a village, strengthen bonds, and create lasting support—because together, the Marine Corps community is stronger.
